**Explanation:** The `hashlib` documentation has a warning that says "Some algorithms have known hash collision weaknesses (including MD5 and SHA1)." The docs name only these two, so I list only these two, though "including" suggests the list is not exhaustive. Keyed hashing for message authentication is provided by the `hmac` module, whose title reads "Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication". `hashlib`'s BLAKE2 also has its own built-in keyed mode, which the docs describe as a faster and simpler replacement for HMAC. The dedicated keyed-hashing module is still `hmac`.
